results.proposal_summary: The DIGITWIN4CIUE Reduction-Fees Scholarships programme, launched by Fundación Agustín de Betancourt (FUNAB) and co-financed 50% by the European Union under the Digital Europe Programme, provides partial tuition fee waivers of €1,500–€3,000 per year to individual students enrolled full-time in the Executive Master in Digital Twins for Infrastructures and Cities for the 2025–2026 academic year. Eligible applicants must be nationals of EEA countries or countries associated with the Digital Europe Programme, accepted into and enrolled in the master's programme, and committed to completing it in the first year of enrolment. Selection is based on a merit score (1–5) reflecting academic/professional experience, CV, and motivation letter, with priority given to female applicants, students from EIT Regional Innovation Scheme countries, affiliated HEI students, and self-financed students. The submission deadline was 31 October 2025. The ILO is not an eligible applicant as this call targets individual students only, and the maximum grant amount of €3,000 is below the USD 50,000 threshold.

results.title: Adaptation Benefit Mechanism (ABM) - African Development Bank
theme: Just Transitions towards Environmentally Sustainable Economies and Societies
results.proposal_summary: The Adaptation Benefit Mechanism (ABM) is an African Development Bank initiative designed to mobilise public and private finance for climate change adaptation in Africa by certifying and assigning value to adaptation benefits. The mechanism operates through a pilot phase (2019-2023) that has now concluded, with plans to establish a permanent secretariat by 2027. The ABM functions as a financial intermediation tool, issuing certificates for verified adaptation benefits to project developers and promoting these to potential investors or lenders, rather than providing direct grants to implementing organisations. No open call for proposals with a defined deadline or application window is currently active on this page.
results.ilo_match_evidence: While the ABM touches on climate resilience and includes some activities related to decent work outcomes (job creation for vulnerable groups), its primary purpose is financial market mobilisation for climate adaptation investment, which falls outside the ILO's mandate for technical assistance and labour standards work.

results.proposal_summary: The ADF Climate Action Window is an initiative of the African Development Fund (concessional arm of the African Development Bank Group) established under its 16th replenishment cycle to help fill the climate finance gap for low-income African countries. Resources are allocated across three sub-windows: 75% for adaptation, 15% for mitigation, and 10% for technical assistance, covering six thematic sectors including agriculture and food security, water security, climate information, green transport, green energy, and green finance. The programme targets ADF-eligible sub-Saharan and North African countries, offering a large grant component to minimise debt distress. This landing page does not present a currently open call with a defined deadline; eligible applicant types and specific grant amounts are not specified on this page.
results.ilo_match_evidence: While the technical assistance sub-window could theoretically support policy and capacity-building activities relevant to just transitions, the programme is primarily a development finance investment vehicle for climate projects in Africa, with no explicit alignment to labour standards, decent work, or social protection objectives.

results.proposal_summary: The Africa Adaptation Acceleration Program (AAAP) is a joint initiative of the African Development Bank and the Global Center on Adaptation aiming to mobilise USD 25 billion over five years to accelerate climate adaptation across Africa. It operates through four pillars covering digital agriculture, infrastructure resilience, youth green entrepreneurship, and innovative adaptation finance. Implementation channels include an upstream financing facility at GCA and the ADF Climate Action Window for low-income countries. results.proposal_summary: The Africa Climate Change Fund (ACCF) is a multi-donor trust fund managed by the African Development Bank, established in 2014 with contributions from Germany, Belgium (Flanders), Italy, Canada, Austria, Ireland, the USA, the Province of Quebec, and the Global Center on Adaptation. It provides small grants to African governments, NGOs, and regional institutions to support climate-resilient, low-carbon development across Africa, including NDC implementation, capacity building for climate finance access, and adaptation/mitigation actions. No specific open call, deadline, grant size range, or application mechanism is described on this page — it is a general programme description/landing page for the ACCF initiative.
results.ilo_match_evidence: The ACCF focuses on climate resilience and environmental transitions in Africa, which has partial overlap with ILO's just transition mandate, but the fund's primary focus is climate finance, NDCs, and adaptation/mitigation rather than labour standards, employment, or social protection, and ILO is ineligible as an applicant.

results.proposal_summary: Switzerland's State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) launched the third call for proposals on 28 May 2026, inviting Swiss private-sector companies with an established presence in Ukraine to submit investment project proposals focused on constructing or reconstructing facilities for long-term production and/or operations in Ukraine. The federal government will co-finance selected projects with amounts ranging from CHF 3 million to CHF 10 million per project, drawing on a CHF 500 million envelope within Switzerland's Ukraine country programme 2025–2028. Applicants must contribute at least 50% of the required funding. Projects will be selected through a two-stage process by a Swiss-Ukrainian committee, with the selection procedure running until spring 2027. Eligibility is strictly limited to Swiss companies; the deadline for submission is 20 September 2026.

results.proposal_summary: The Common Fund for Commodities (CFC) has launched its 29th Call for Proposals, inviting applications from SMEs, cooperatives, social enterprises, NGOs, and public or private sector entities based or operating in one of the 101 CFC member countries. The call focuses on transformative projects that empower smallholder farmers and strengthen communities through trade finance, regenerative agriculture, local value addition, agtech, financial access, and women's entrepreneurship. Funding is provided exclusively as loans and other debt instruments, with a maximum of USD 1.5 million per regular project (or USD 300,000 under the Fast-Track procedure). Priority is given to projects in the Congo Basin region and in Least Developed, Landlocked Developing, and Small Island Developing Countries. Applicants must have a minimum of 3 years of operational history. The submission deadline is 1 October 2026. The ILO is not eligible as this call targets private sector and civil society entities and provides debt financing rather than grants.
results.ilo_match_evidence: While the call touches on smallholder livelihoods, gender inclusion, and decent work indicators, its primary purpose is private-sector investment through loans to agribusinesses, which does not align with the ILO's mandate of technical assistance, labour standards, and policy work.
